bullet_points: Load the QM9 dataset from /home/node/work/data/qm9/qm9.csv.
Parse the SMILES strings using RDKit.
Identify the 83 duplicated SMILES (stereochemistry collapsed) and handle them by averaging their target property values (u0, gap, mu, homo, lumo) to ensure consistency.
Calculate heavy atom counts and implicit hydrogen counts for each molecule using RDKit.
Derive element count vectors, specific bond-type count vectors, and compute per-heavy-atom u0.
Save the cleaned and augmented dataframe to data/cleaned_qm9.csv (or .pkl).
Load the cleaned dataset from data/.
Using the derived element and bond-type count vectors as additive features, train separate Ridge regression models to predict u0, gap, and mu.
Calculate the residuals (actual minus predicted) for each of these three properties.
Plot the residuals against heavy atom counts to verify size independence; if scaling remains for u0, normalize the residuals by the number of heavy atoms.
Save the computed residuals, the additive features array, and the size-independence plots (e.g., data/residuals_vs_size.png) to the data/ directory.
Load the dataset with additive features and computed residuals from Step 2.
Train a Random Forest or XGBoost regressor strictly on the same additive features to predict the computed residuals for u0, gap, and mu.
Evaluate the performance (MSE, R2) of these models on a standard train/test split to establish a non-linear baseline.
Save the performance metrics (e.g., data/baseline_metrics.txt) and baseline predictions to the data/ directory.

sub_tasks.sub_task: Advanced Feature Engineering and Scaffold Split
bullet_points: Load the cleaned dataset and the target residuals.
Generate Morgan fingerprints (radius 2 or 3) and standard RDKit 2D descriptors for each molecule to capture extended topological motifs (replacing explicit graph construction).
Perform a scaffold split using RDKit to divide the data into training, validation, and test sets to test generalization across molecular architectures.
Apply StandardScaler to the residuals to stabilize downstream model training.
Save the engineered features, the target scalers, and the split indices to the data/ directory.
Load the split datasets and topological features from Step 4.

Implement an advanced non-linear model (e.g., XGBoost with GPU tree method or a pure PyTorch MLP). If using PyTorch, explicitly check torch.cuda.mem_get_info() to ensure the batch fits within the VRAM budget, falling back to CPU if unavailable.
Train the model on the training set to predict the scaled residuals, using the validation set for early stopping to prevent overfitting.
Evaluate the model on the test set, computing MSE and R2.
Save the trained model, training curves, and test set predictions to the data/ directory.
Load the trained topological model and the test set features from Step 5.
Compute SHAP values for the Morgan fingerprints/descriptors to attribute the predicted non-additive residuals to specific topological sub-structures and functional groups.
Calculate and aggregate the mean absolute SHAP values for each feature across the test set.
Save the SHAP attribution arrays and a summary table of the most influential structural motifs (e.g., data/shap_motif_summary.csv) to the data/ directory.
Load the test set predictions, intensive properties (gap, mu, homo, lumo), and the SHAP motif summary from the previous steps.
Compute correlation matrices (Pearson/Spearman) between the predicted energetic residuals and the intensive properties.
Group molecules based on the presence of the highest-influence structural motifs identified by SHAP (e.g., specific conjugation patterns or rings).
Calculate descriptive statistics (mean, variance) for gap and mu across these specific motif groups to quantify deviations from classical group-contribution theory.
Save the correlation matrices and the aggregated motif statistics dataframes to data/.
Load the correlation matrices and aggregated motif statistics from Step 7.
Generate scatter plots visualizing the correlation between non-additive energy residuals and intensive properties (gap, mu).
Create bar or box plots comparing the distributions of gap and mu across the high-influence motif groups.
Save all generated plots (e.g., data/residual_gap_corr.png, data/motif_distributions.png) to the data/ directory.
Review all metrics, tables, and plots saved in the data/ directory by the engineer across the previous steps.
Write a comprehensive Results section for the final research report.
Discuss the performance of the baseline additive models and non-linear baseline in isolating extensive energetics versus the topological models.
Interpret the SHAP attributions, identifying specifically which structural motifs (e.g., extended π-conjugation) govern non-additive energetic stability.
Analyze the correlations between structural non-additivities and intensive properties (gap, mu), explicitly referencing the specific generated plots and statistics files by their paths in data/.
Synthesize how these empirical findings successfully decouple extensive scaling from intrinsic electronic physics.
